rationale.conceptual: Using ReaxFF with cellulose is an established method, but the reactive force field, model building for amorphous cellulose, and extraction of elastic constants from stress-strain curves require a non-trivial understanding of the force field and MD protocols. Not a novel algorithm, but several interacting components that need careful implementation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of 5 sequential MD stages (structure build, minimize, NPT equilibrate, tensile deformation, property extraction), each with specific input scripts, file I/O, and long simulation times. Orchestrating LAMMPS with the correct ReaxFF parameter file and handling trajectory data adds moderate engineering complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies an established reactive force field (ReaxFF) to model amorphous cellulose mechanical properties. The method is standard within molecular dynamics, though the reactive bond-breaking capability and proper equilibration/deformation protocol require careful implementation. Conceptual difficulty is moderate (non-trivial but not novel). The reproduction pipeline involves 5 stages (structure generation, minimization, equilibration, deformation, property extraction) with tool-specific scripting and long simulation runs, making execution moderately complex.

compute_estimate.reasoning: ReaxFF MD on ~28k atoms with 0.5 fs timestep, 250 ps equilibration plus deformation; the expensive force field makes a single A100-class GPU necessary for practical runtime. Memory ~8 GB suffices for the system and force field; input data (force field file, initial structure) is negligible (<0.01 GB).
